data.name: Kaspar
data.gender_notes: Kaspar is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word ‘kaspar’, meaning treasurer or royal advisor. In the Bible, Kaspar is one of the Magi who visited the infant Jesus. The name Kaspar carries the meaning “Treasurer, Royal Advisor” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kaspar usually hope their child will grow to embody treasurer, royal advisor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kaspar belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Treasurer, Royal Advisor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kaspar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: כָסְפָר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'kaphar' meaning 'to hide, to cover'. The name Kaspar is derived from the word 'kaspa' meaning 'box, chest, treasury'. This name is biblical and refers to a wise man from the East who came to worship the infant Jesus (Matthew 2:1-12).

in_greek.name: Κασπαρ
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'kasparos' meaning 'treasurer, box, chest'. This name is derived from the Hebrew name 'Kaspar'. The name is biblical and is mentioned in the New Testament as the name of one of the magi who came to worship Jesus (Matthew 2:1-12).

in_latin.name: Caspar
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'caspar' meaning 'treasurer, box, chest'. This name is derived from the Greek name 'Kasparos' and the Hebrew name 'Kaspar'. The name is biblical and is mentioned in the New Testament as the name of one of the magi who came to worship Jesus (Matthew 2:1-12).

data.cultural_impact: In Christian tradition, Kaspar is revered as one of the Three Wise Men, the Magi who followed a star to Bethlehem and brought gifts to the infant Jesus. The name Kaspar has therefore come to symbolize travel, adventure, and the pursuit of knowledge, with its association with the Magi's journey.
data.spiritual_significance: Kaspar is a reminder of the spiritual journey we each embark on in life, seeking the truth and wisdom that can only be found through faith and following the guidance of God, like the Magi followed the star. It is a name that instills a sense of purpose and direction, leading us on our own personal pilgrimage to knowledge, understanding, and ultimately, enlightenment.
